typology_delta.finding: E 11072 belongs to the specialized architectural type 'base du reliquaire abydénien': a lion-protome base supporting a shaft/hampe, above which sat the Abydos Osiris reliquary basket/chest with tall plumes.
typology_delta.meaning: The missing elements should no longer be modeled as an arbitrary upper/lower box mate. The reconstruction target is a vertical reliquary architecture: lion base -> shaft/hampe -> reliquary basket/chest -> tall plumes.

barguet_1952.citation: Paul Barguet, La base du Reliquaire abydénien, Revue d'Egyptologie 9 (1952), 153-155
barguet_1952.relevance: Dedicated publication on Louvre E 11072; bibliographic indexing explicitly links E11072 with Osiris/Abydos/relic/head context. Full text still desirable for exact reconstruction details.

heka_2000.relevance: Louvre exhibition catalogue identifies E 11072 specifically as 'Base du reliquaire d'Abydos', Saite period (?), diorite, H 14.6 cm, W 11.7 cm.

provenance_contradiction.current_louvre_record: Acquired in 1905 from the Dosseurs, objects previously ceded by Maurice Nahman.
provenance_contradiction.secondary_historical_chain: Rossini 2016, citing Perdrizet 1921-22, states that Louvre E 11072 was acquired in 1908 from Soliman through the antiquary Cassira and Emile Chassinat.
provenance_contradiction.importance: These chains are not chronologically or actor-wise equivalent. Until the underlying 1905 and alleged 1908 documents are inspected, neither should be silently merged.
possible_explanations_to_test: Rossini/Perdrizet attribution conflates E 11072 with another lion-protome base.
Current Louvre provenance was revised from later archival evidence.
The 1905 batch record and 1908 narrative refer to different acquisition stages or different objects.
A legacy inventory-number attribution error exists in secondary scholarship.

archive_route.reference_family: Archives nationales 20144775, Département des Antiquités égyptiennes du Louvre
archive_route.confirmed_context: 20144775/8 is a broad container with nineteenth-century material, including Mariette correspondence and an 1832 Hauterive acquisition; the range therefore cannot itself be treated as proof of the 1905 transaction.
required_document_targets: Nahman-to-Dosseur transfer description or attached object list
